concepts.text: Recalling information without looking at the source strengthens later recall.
Practice distributed across separate days reduces forgetting.
Checking an answer against the source reveals missing ideas that need correction.

questions.question: What study action helps you remember the material later?
questions.expected_answer: Attempt to recall information without looking at the source.

questions.question: Why should you try answering before reopening your notes?
questions.expected_answer: Recalling without looking strengthens later recall.

questions.question: A learner studies a topic once and forgets it. How should they arrange further practice?
questions.expected_answer: Distribute practice across separate days to reduce forgetting.

questions.question: After giving an answer, how can you find what your explanation missed?
questions.expected_answer: Check the answer against the source to reveal missing ideas.

questions.question: Your explanation leaves out one idea from the source. What should you do after comparing them?
questions.expected_answer: Identify and correct the missing idea revealed by source checking.
